children: The following are expectations for the resumption of grain and soy complex trading at the Chicago Board of Trade at 8:30 a.m. CDT (1330 GMT) on Monday.
WHEAT - Up 5 to 7 cents per bushel
higher on worries about tightening global supplies amid ongoing disruptions to Russian and Ukrainian exports.
Agriculture consultancy APK-Inform increased its 2026 Ukrainian grain harvest forecast, but cut its estimate for grain exports from the country this year due to a blockade of key Black Sea ports.
Algeria's state grains agency OAIC issued a tender to buy optional-origin soft milling wheat, traders said.

CBOT December soft red winter wheat (WZ26) was last up 5-1/2 cents at $7.30-3/4 per bushel. K.C. December hard red winter wheat (KWZ26) was unchanged at $7.98-1/2 a bushel. Minneapolis December spring wheat (MWEZ26) was last 2 cents higher at $7.47 a bushel.
CORN - Steady to up 2 cents per bushel
futures steady to firm after the USDA cut its U.S. harvest outlook on Friday. Spillover support from rising crude oil also kept a floor under grain prices.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture lowered its U.S. corn harvest outlook on Friday after hot summertime weather led to concerns about crop damage.
CBOT December corn (CZ26) was last up 3/4 cent at $5.31 per bushel.
SOYBEANS - Up 1 to 3 cents per bushel

firm in a rebound from a steep drop on Friday. Hopes for continued Chinese import demand ahead of a meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping next week underpinned prices.
The USDA on Friday raised its U.S. soybean production forecast after increasing its average yield and harvested acres outlooks.
CBOT November soybeans (SX26) were last up 2-1/4 cents at $12.98-3/4 per bushel.
